title: The Open Window
summary: A nervous visitor is told a ghostly story by a young girl, and the evening ends with a clever surprise.

chapters.title: A Calm Cure
sentences: Framton Nuttel had come to the countryside because his doctor wanted him to rest his fragile nerves.
His sister had given him several letters of introduction, and he delivered the first one with little enthusiasm.
He was shown into a quiet drawing room, where a calm girl of fifteen greeted him politely.
Her aunt, she explained, would be down shortly, so he would have to endure her company until then.
Framton tried to say something charming, though he doubted that these visits would help his health.
The girl glanced at the large window that stood wide open onto the lawn, even though it was October.
She asked whether he knew anything about the family, and he admitted that he knew almost nothing.
Then she lowered her voice and said that something terrible had happened in that very room three years before.
Her aunt's husband and two brothers had gone shooting across the swamp and had never returned.
They had disappeared in the soft ground, and their bodies had never been found, which was the cruelest part.
Her aunt still believed they would walk back one evening, followed by their little brown dog.
That was why the window stayed open every day until the light had completely faded.

quiz.q: Why did Framton come to the countryside?
quiz.explain: His doctor wanted him to rest his fragile nerves.

quiz.q: What does the girl claim happened three years earlier?
options: Three men vanished on a hunting trip.
quiz.explain: She says her aunt's husband and brothers never returned from the swamp.

quiz.q: Why is the window left open?
options: Her aunt expects the men to return.
quiz.explain: The aunt believes they will walk back one evening.

chapters.title: The Return
sentences: Soon the aunt hurried in, apologised for the delay, and chatted cheerfully about the weather and the birds.
Framton tried to answer politely, but the girl's story kept returning to his mind with growing fear.
The aunt mentioned that her husband and brothers would soon be back from shooting, and she hoped they would not bring too much mud.
Framton, trying to be sympathetic, explained as gently as he could that doctors had advised him to avoid all excitement.
The aunt barely listened, because she was staring at the open window with a bright and expectant smile.
Framton turned and saw three figures crossing the lawn in the dusk, with guns under their arms and a dog beside them.
One of them sang a cheerful tune, and the sight was more than his shaken nerves could tolerate.
He grabbed his hat and walking stick, and ran from the house without even saying goodbye.
The men entered the room, puzzled, and the aunt remarked that the visitor had behaved very oddly.
The girl offered a quick explanation: he had been bitten by dogs in India and feared them ever since.
She could invent a tale on any subject, and she did so with perfect calm and no visible effort.
For her, romance at short notice was a gift, and the poor man was only her latest audience.

options: He was late for a train.
quiz.explain: He believed the three men crossing the lawn were the vanished hunters.

quiz.q: What excuse did the girl give for his behaviour?
quiz.explain: She said he had been bitten by dogs in India.

quiz.q: What does the ending show about the girl?
options: She tells convincing invented stories easily.
She is deeply afraid of ghosts.
quiz.explain: She invents a tale at short notice with perfect calm.
